author: ribeye
dek: Apple's first folding iPhone starts at $1,999, and one Sandusky family is trying to figure out what else two grand buys on the Lake Erie shore.
disclaimer: Parody: the Kowalski family of Sandusky is fictional. The unveiling of Apple's foldable iPhone Duo is real, as reported by the Associated Press in September 2026.
headline: Sandusky Dad Does the Math: New Folding iPhone Costs More Than a Summer at Cedar Point

ohio_story: SANDUSKY, Ohio — Mark Kowalski had been saving for a new phone since spring, and he had a plan: wait for the September Apple event, watch it on the living-room TV with a bowl of Toft's ice cream, and then make a responsible adult decision. The plan survived about eleven minutes. "Two thousand dollars," he said, staring at the folding phone on the screen. "That's a Cedar Point season pass for the whole family, plus the meal plan, plus parking, and I'd still have money left over for the drive-thru at the end of the pier."

His wife, Denise, was less impressed by the folding part and more impressed by the price tag. She pointed out that their current phones still work fine, that the kids have already cracked two screens this year between the Blue Streaks football games and the Lake Erie beach, and that a phone that folds in half is, in her words, "just twice as many ways for a teenager to break it." Their daughter, 15-year-old Grace, disagreed on every point, noting that the Duo's giant screen would be perfect for watching Buckeyes highlights in the Cedar Point line for Steel Vengeance, and that she had already worked out a payment plan involving her birthday money, her babysitting money, and what she described as "a small loan from the Tooth Fairy, retroactively."

By Thursday morning, the Kowalskis had reached a compromise, the way Sandusky families always do: nobody is buying a $1,999 phone, but Mark is allowed to go look at one when it comes out in October, and Grace is allowed to come along, provided she leaves her wallet in the car. "It's a beautiful piece of technology," Mark said, folding his own phone shut — it does not fold, and never will — "but it doesn't fold into a boat, and it doesn't get you on Millennium Force any faster."
real_summary: Apple on Wednesday, Sept. 9, 2026, unveiled its latest generation of iPhones, including a widely anticipated foldable version called Duo. The company's new CEO, John Ternus, who took over from Tim Cook on Sept. 1, introduced the lineup at Apple's Cupertino, California, headquarters, telling the audience inside the Steve Jobs Theater that "actually there is one more thing," in a nod to the trademark phrase of the company's late founder, Steve Jobs.

The Duo opens to a 7.6-inch display that is 80 percent larger than the newest iPhone 18 Pro, which Ternus called the largest display ever on an iPhone, "yet fits into your pocket." It will let people use an Apple Pencil on the phone, a capability previously reserved for iPad users, and split the screen to use two different apps, or two windows of the same website for things like comparison shopping. With a starting price of $1,999, it is the most expensive iPhone yet, and it will be available on Oct. 23.

Apple also announced the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max, starting at $1,199 and $1,299 respectively, with preorders beginning Sept. 12 and availability Sept. 18. Many of Apple's biggest rivals, such as Samsung, Motorola and Google, have already come out with foldable smartphones. Ben Wood, chief analyst at CCS Insight, said the Duo "was always going to eclipse Apple's other announcements at the event," while noting that foldables still account for less than 5 percent of the overall smartphone market. The iPhone 18 costs about $100 more than earlier generations, due partly to a global memory chip shortage.
source_note: AP reporting, Sep 9, 2026: Apple unveils the foldable iPhone Duo and the iPhone 18 lineup; new CEO John Ternus; $1,999 starting price; Oct. 23 availability.
